answer: Identity is bound to a signed measurement of the runtime that produced it, so two identities reporting the same measurement are counted as one voice no matter how many keys or balances sit behind them. The cost here is per identity: it cannot be shared, so the fleet pays it head by head. The pulse is the quoted measurement, the terrace the group it forms, and the violet the voice that group is worth; the pulse and the terrace collapse a farm, while only a fresh violet of hardware escapes the grouping. Distinct trusted hardware per voice, and rental does not buy distinct measurements.
